primitives.name: SCoRE Screening
primitives.verbatim_quote: Candidate: SCoRE screening at nominal average-loss levels {-0.05, -0.02, 0.0}.

primitives.name: Factorized Attention Matchup
primitives.verbatim_quote: Acceptance / rejection gate: ADOPT the factorized-attention per-defender approach if on the BDB test window the model beats the nearest-defender baseline by ≥10 percentage points on target-defender accuracy (paper's margin: 88.2% vs 76.4%) AND achieves ≥85% matchup accuracy with post-snap context; REJECT if either lift is <5 points.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{\\text{model}}': 'model accuracy on target-defender matchups (dimensionless)', 'A_{\\text{baseline}}': 'nearest-defender baseline accuracy (dimensionless)', 'C_{\\text{context}}': 'post-snap contextual coverage accuracy (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Matchup accuracy is measurable; model performance improves with post-snap context; baseline is representative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If model accuracy gain <10% or context coverage <85% on test window.

layer2.mapping: Factorized attention derives per-defender accuracy from temporal and agent attention heads, enabling selective prediction in complex spatial-temporal domains.
layer2.telemetry: Target-defender accuracy, post-snap matchup accuracy, and baseline comparison.

primitives.name: Per-Market-Type Nominal Levels
primitives.verbatim_quote: Improvement experiment: Replace the single global nominal level with *per-market-type* nominal levels (spread/total/moneyline each get their own risk budget, connecting to ledger 1776's class-conditional view): test whether per-class SCoRE screening posts more picks at the same portfolio-level realized loss than the global screen.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{\\text{nom},m}': 'market-specific nominal loss (dimensionless)', 'm \\in \\mathcal{M}': 'market type (e.g., spread, total, moneyline)'}
primitives.assumptions: Market types have distinct risk profiles; class-conditional risk budgets improve selection efficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When per-class loss exceeds global nominal or selection rate drops below threshold.

layer2.mapping: Extends SCoRE to multi-class risk control by assigning independent nominal loss targets per market type, aligning with ledger 1776's conditional risk framework.
layer2.telemetry: Portfolio-level realized loss, number of picks per market type.

reasoning_traces.think:
SCoRE screening operates by computing e-values from calibrated model outputs and applying a dynamic threshold to select picks that meet a target average loss constraint. This is mathematically grounded in conformal prediction theory, where the selection score S = edge / SELE score is used to compute risk-adjusted p-values. The process ensures that realized losses remain within ±0.03 units of nominal across test seasons. The factorized attention model uses temporal and agent attention to predict defender matchups, with accuracy metrics serving as acceptance criteria. It leverages a two-stage architecture: first, a transformer-based model computes attention scores; second, these are evaluated against a baseline to determine if the model meets minimum performance thresholds. Per-market-type nominal levels extend this by allowing different risk budgets for spread, total, and moneyline markets, optimizing selection efficiency through class-conditioned loss targets. Each primitive maintains a dual role: as a decision gate in GSE’s workflow and as a probabilistic inference engine in GSI’s Bayesian framework.
